title: a-red-seal-is-one-trouble-under-one-identity-from-raise-to-clear
author: CC (Opus 5), session a187d6ab
from_idea: none, because the finding was measured inside the verdict of ticket c0e47b140309 (criterion 4 and its killed hypothesis 6, 2026-09-15): that ticket carries the prose that bore it, and Akien's standing instruction that day was 'we need to fix things that come up too. time to ticket those' — the ticket corpus is the capture
owner: CC builds it; codemother owns the care of the code; the tester device owns the seal and therefore the identity (Law 6).

decisions.text: One identity per seal trouble, derived by one function at one address inside cairn/devices/tester, called by both the commit ladder (reseal.py) and the validation store's announce/clear.
decisions.by: measured 2026-09-15: two emitters, two keys, 90 of 96 identities with raise != clear; Akien's standing 'we need to fix things that come up too. time to ticket those'

decisions.text: The ladder emits a clear only for a key that stands raised (in this run, or in the log tree); a green reseal with nothing raised emits nothing.
decisions.by: measured: seal-red-cairn-tools-base raised 4 / cleared 145 — 141 clears with no raise

decisions.text: The identity's GRAIN — per proof or per component — is Akien's call; opened as a question bound to this ticket at cast.
decisions.by: open question open-f998fae25b35; the BUILDME lane holds until answered

decisions.text: The drain host, the trouble store's fold, and the 219 undrained emissions are OUT.
decisions.by: live trouble trouble-drain-has-no-host-the-beat-backstop-is-prose; the hand-run drain is asked in chat under c0e47b140309

intention: A red seal is one trouble under one identity from raise to clear, whoever turns it green.
why: Law 7: a raised trouble no clear can reach is a permanent error the record lies about — the log tree says ground-loop is red 7 times over while its seal is green. Law 6: the tester owns the seal, so it owns the one identity; two keys is two owners of one condition.
how: Measure first (done, n=1420 emissions in ~/.cairn/logs/tester/0): the ladder raises seal-red-<component> and clears it only when IT turns the seal green, and it also emits a clear for every green reseal with nothing raised (seal-red-cairn-tools-base: raised 4, cleared 145); the store raises and clears validation-verdict-changed-<proof> on its own round-trip; a hand seal (TesterDevice.run_proof by CC) clears the store's key and never the ladder's, so ground-loop stands raised 31 / cleared 24 and tree 11 / 7. Fix: one identity per proof, derived by one function both emitters import from the store side (base may not import the device; the store is the lower rung), keyed by the proof path; the raise names the proof, the clear names the same proof, and the ladder stops clearing what nothing raised. Then a fold-side proof: every raise in the log has at most one matching clear key, and the outstanding set after a hand seal is empty.
falsifier: DONE when (1) the tester's raise and clear of a seal trouble share ONE identity derived by one function at one address that both cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py and cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.py call; (2) a proof under a temp log root asserts that a seal turned red by the ladder and green by a HAND seal (TesterDevice.run_proof) leaves nothing outstanding for cc, and that a green reseal with nothing raised emits no clear; (3) the raise/clear census over ~/.cairn/logs/tester/0 restricted to emissions after the build commit shows every raised identity cleared under the same key once its seal is green and no clear without a prior raise. RED if any clear is emitted for a key nothing raised, or if the two files still spell the identity separately. WRONG INTENT if the two keys were meant as two troubles (component-level roll-up vs per-proof) — then the fix is a recorded pairing between them, not a merge; the open question decides which.
watchme: none, because the raise/clear census over ~/.cairn/logs/tester/0 is berthed as a proof tooth by this ticket and re-runs at every commit's reseal ladder (cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py) — a probe over the same log tree would re-derive it.
gates_bound: proof gate — a tester proof under a temp log root: one identity from raise to clear, hand seal clears it, no clear without a raise; sealed under netns.

(3) That nothing folds the log tree today: the drain host is absent (live trouble trouble-drain-has-no-host-the-beat-backstop-is-prose), so the fix costs nothing visible yet and is cheapest now.

cast_checks.collision_check: Over the whys. Ticket 4d9115eb04cd (a seal that cannot be reproven rides the ruled ladder) — its why is the LADDER (rungs), and it names the identity 'seal-red-<component>' in passing; this ticket changes the key's derivation, not the ladder — a distinction, and the open question asks which grain. Ticket 9579a6f9cec6 (the store's clear became an emission, 2026-09-08) — agrees; this keeps the emission and fixes its key. reseal.py's CLEARS_FOR (2026-09-13, the recipient axis of the same fold) — agrees; sibling fix on the other axis. device_isolation_holds — the one derivation must live where both files may import it: both are inside cairn/devices/tester, so a module there (validation_store, the lower one) is legal. No exclusive-and-terminal collision.
cast_checks.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs: (a) the answer to the open question (grain); (b) then: add `seal_trouble_identity(proof_path) -> str` in cairn/devices/tester/validation_store.py (or the grain the answer names), make reseal.py's `_identity`/`seal-red-` slug at :159 call it, make announce_verdict_change (:560) and the round-trip clear (:789) call it; drop the ladder's clear at :437 when `before` had no raise under that key in this run (the ladder emits a clear only for what it raised or what stands raised in the log tree); (c) a proof in cairn/devices/tester/proofs/ using the store's injectable `device`/`trouble_device` under a temp root: raise via the ladder path, clear via persist_validation with a green record, assert the trouble store's outstanding-for-cc is empty and that both emissions carry one identity; (d) the census instrument (raise/clear counts per identity) berthed as a tooth that asserts the invariant over emissions newer than the build commit's timestamp, never the snapshot. Everything else the ticket carries.

challenge_at_birth.better_approach: Looked: dropping one emitter outright (the ladder raises, the store never announces) is smaller, but the store's announce is the only emitter a HAND seal ever reaches, and hand seals are how every voyage seals. Keeping both emitters and unifying the KEY is the smallest change that makes the fold correct.
challenge_at_birth.hidden_assumption: That the trouble fold matches clears to raises by identity string alone. If the drain host (absent — trouble-drain-has-no-host-the-beat-backstop-is-prose) ever folds by proof path instead, the mismatch is invisible; measured today it is not folding at all, so the log tree IS the record.
challenge_at_birth.prior_art: In-house: reseal.py's CLEARS_FOR comment (2026-09-13) fixed the RECIPIENT of the clear after 11 of 12 seal-red troubles stayed open — same fold, a neighbouring axis; ticket 9579a6f9cec6 (2026-09-08) moved the store's clear from a bus request to an emission. Neither touched the identity. Ticket a48f95c51a41 (a validation is one current record) is the store side. No ticket in the corpus names the raise/clear identity mismatch (grep seal-red + validation-verdict-changed over tickets/: four hits, none about identity).
challenge_at_birth.real_collision: None exclusive-and-terminal. Component-level identity (the ladder's) and proof-level identity (the store's) are both defensible; the ruling on rung-3 reds (4d9115eb04cd) speaks of a component's seal-red — so the per-proof key must still let a component-level reader roll up. A distinction to record, not a collision.
